property.name: ElapsedGameTime
property.summary: The amount of elapsed game time since the last update.
property.remarks: Fixed-step clocks update by a fixed time span upon every clock step. This results in uniform clock steps that may not actually track the wall clock time. Fixed-step clocks were popular on console systems where one had tight control over code and a fixed system performance. Fixed-step clocks are also useful when trying to achieve deterministic updates for debugging, offline rendering, or other such scenarios.

property.name: ElapsedRealTime
property.summary: The amount of elapsed real time (wall clock) since the last frame.
property.remarks: Variable-step clocks automatically track the difference in real-time (wall clock) that transpired since the last clock step. This type of game timing is popular on PC games where the variable PC configurations affect update time.

property.name: IsRunningSlowly
property.summary: Gets a value indicating that the game loop is taking longer than its TargetElapsedTime. In this case, the game loop can be considered to be running too slowly and should do something to "catch up."
